factors.name: Requirement stability
factors.rationale: Draft or unapproved requirements indicate that stability has not yet been demonstrated.

factors.name: Requirement clarity
factors.rationale: Measured from the presence of concrete, non-placeholder acceptance criteria.

factors.name: Risk
factors.rationale: Derived from stated high risk and security, privacy, regulatory, or audit classifications.

factors.name: Complexity
factors.rationale: Integration and data-management requirements increase coordination and technical complexity.

factors.name: Need for early prototype
factors.rationale: Unclear requirements or integration complexity make early learning and validation valuable.

factors.name: Time constraints
factors.rationale: No schedule or deadline evidence is available in the generated requirements; confirm this with the project sponsor.

factors.name: Customer involvement
factors.rationale: Derived only from business, stakeholder, or usability requirements; otherwise this must be confirmed.

factors.name: Frequency of changes
factors.rationale: Requirement documents do not establish the expected change rate; confirm with product and business stakeholders.

factors.name: Need for iterative development
factors.rationale: Unapproved or unclear requirements benefit from repeated review and validation cycles.

factors.name: Need for risk analysis
factors.rationale: Security/compliance concerns or complex integration warrant explicit risk analysis.

options.name: Spiral
options.suitability: Best when risk analysis, prototypes, and repeated risk-reduction cycles are central.

options.name: Prototyping
options.suitability: Best for validating uncertain user needs, workflows, and interfaces before committing to a full build.

options.name: Agile
options.suitability: Best for frequent feedback and evolving requirements, with planned governance for high-risk work.

options.name: Incremental
options.suitability: Best when value can be divided into validated, independently testable increments.

options.name: V-Shape
options.suitability: Best when each specification stage needs a linked verification and validation activity.

options.name: RAD
options.suitability: Best for time-boxed delivery with available users and modular, lower-risk scope.

options.name: Waterfall
options.suitability: Best when requirements are stable, fully specified, and changes are controlled.

sdlc.justification: Spiral has the highest transparent score because requirement stability is needs validation, requirement clarity is low, risk is high, complexity is high, need for early prototype is likely.
